subject: Biology
title: Microbes in Human Welfare
summary: Microbes are used at home (curd, bread, idli, dosa), in industry (beverages, antibiotics, organic acids, enzymes, bioactive molecules), in sewage treatment, biogas production, biocontrol and as biofertilisers.
Sewage is treated in two stages: primary (physical removal of solids) and secondary/biological (aerobic microbes form flocs in aeration tanks; anaerobic digestion of activated sludge gives biogas).
Biocontrol uses natural predators and pathogens instead of chemical pesticides; biofertilisers (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, cyanobacteria, mycorrhiza) enrich soil nutrients.

formulas.name: Household products
formulas.formula: curd — Lactobacillus (LAB) converts milk to curd and adds vitamin B₁₂;  bread dough — Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's yeast, CO₂);  Swiss cheese — Propionibacterium sharmanii (large holes from CO₂);  Roquefort cheese — fungi for flavour

formulas.name: Beverages
formulas.formula: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (brewer's yeast) ferments malted cereals and fruit juices → ethanol;  wine and beer without distillation;  whisky, brandy, rum by distillation

formulas.name: Antibiotics
formulas.formula: penicillin — Penicillium notatum (Alexander Fleming, while working on Staphylococci; full potential shown by Chain and Florey)

formulas.name: Organic acids and alcohol
formulas.formula: citric acid — Aspergillus niger;  acetic acid — Acetobacter aceti;  butyric acid — Clostridium butylicum;  lactic acid — Lactobacillus;  ethanol — Saccharomyces cerevisiae

formulas.name: Enzymes and bioactive molecules
formulas.formula: lipases (detergents, remove oily stains);  pectinases and proteases (clarify fruit juices);  streptokinase — Streptococcus (clot buster for myocardial infarction);  cyclosporin A — Trichoderma polysporum (immunosuppressant in transplants);  statins — Monascus purpureus (lower blood cholesterol; competitive inhibitors of cholesterol synthesis)

formulas.name: Sewage treatment
formulas.formula: primary: filtration and sedimentation (primary sludge, effluent);  secondary: aeration tank with flocs (bacteria + fungal filaments) → BOD falls → settling tank (activated sludge) → part returned as inoculum, rest to anaerobic sludge digesters (biogas)

formulas.name: BOD
formulas.formula: biochemical oxygen demand = O₂ consumed if all organic matter in 1 L water were oxidised by bacteria;  higher BOD = more polluted

formulas.name: Biogas
formulas.formula: mainly methane + CO₂ + H₂;  methanogens (Methanobacterium) in cattle dung (gobar) under anaerobic conditions;  slurry used as fertiliser;  technology developed by IARI and KVIC

formulas.name: Biocontrol agents
formulas.formula: ladybird and dragonflies (aphids and mosquitoes);  Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt — butterfly caterpillars);  Trichoderma (fungal plant pathogens);  baculoviruses, genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus (species-specific, narrow spectrum insecticide)

formulas.name: Biofertilisers
formulas.formula: Rhizobium (root nodules of legumes);  Azospirillum, Azotobacter (free-living, fix N₂);  mycorrhiza — Glomus (phosphorus absorption, drought and pathogen resistance);  cyanobacteria — Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria (paddy fields; also add organic matter)

examples.title: Curd from milk
examples.problem: How does a small amount of curd turn milk into curd?
examples.solution: The curd contains Lactobacillus (lactic acid bacteria) that multiply, produce acids that coagulate and partially digest milk proteins, and raise the vitamin B₁₂ content.

examples.title: Heart attack drug
examples.problem: Which microbial product dissolves blood clots in patients with myocardial infarction?
examples.solution: Streptokinase, from the bacterium Streptococcus (modified by genetic engineering).

examples.title: Why is high BOD bad?
examples.problem: Untreated sewage has high BOD. What does that mean?
examples.solution: It contains a lot of biodegradable organic matter; microbes use much dissolved oxygen to break it down, so fish and other aquatic life suffocate.

examples.title: Bt as insecticide
examples.problem: How is Bacillus thuringiensis used against caterpillars?
examples.solution: Dried spores are mixed with water and sprayed on plants; caterpillars eat them, the toxin is released in their gut and kills them, while other insects are unharmed.

examples.title: Organic farming
examples.problem: Why are broad-spectrum pesticides avoided in organic farming?
examples.solution: They kill useful insects and other organisms too; organic farmers want a balanced ecosystem with natural predators that keep pests at manageable levels.

topics.title: Fermented foods
topics.explain: Dough for dosa and idli is fermented by bacteria (puffed-up appearance due to CO₂). Toddy, a traditional drink of southern India, is made by fermenting sap from palms. Fish, soybean and bamboo shoots are fermented too.

topics.title: Microbes in industry
topics.explain: Large vessels called fermentors are used to grow microbes on an industrial scale for beverages, antibiotics and enzymes.

topics.title: Ganga and Yamuna Action Plans
topics.explain: The Ministry of Environment and Forests started Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to save major rivers from pollution, building sewage treatment plants so only treated sewage enters rivers.

topics.title: Integrated pest management
topics.explain: Recognise beneficial organisms (predators and parasites) and pests, understand their life cycles and interactions, and rely as far as possible on natural predation instead of chemicals.

topics.title: Biofertilisers vs chemical fertilisers
topics.explain: Over-use of chemical fertilisers pollutes soil and water; biofertilisers are living organisms that enrich nutrient quality of soil and support organic farming. Many biofertilisers are now commercially available in India.

topics.title: Antibiotics' role
topics.explain: Antibiotics have greatly improved our ability to treat deadly diseases such as plague, whooping cough (kali khansi), diphtheria (gal ghotu) and leprosy (kusht rog).

ratta: Curd — Lactobacillus (B₁₂);  Swiss cheese — Propionibacterium sharmanii.
Citric — Aspergillus niger;  acetic — Acetobacter aceti;  butyric — Clostridium butylicum.
Streptokinase — clot buster;  cyclosporin A — Trichoderma polysporum;  statins — Monascus purpureus.
Penicillin — Fleming;  Chain & Florey proved its use.
